newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen bank shareholders agree rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen bank shareholders agree rights plan.

text.p: Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd said on Wednesday its shareholders had approved the bank's plan to make a 1.5-for-10 rights offer.

The issue, which has been priced at eight yuan per rights share, would be made on the firm's current total share capital of 1.035 billion shares, the bank said in a notice published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
On Monday, the bank's A shares closed at 16.88 yuan per share. Trading in the firm's A shares was suspended on Tuesday pending the announcement of the rights plan.

The firm, the sole bank listed in China, said it aimed to raise more than one billion yuan from the rights offer and use the proceeds to expand its banking network in China and to renovate banking facilities.
The company said the plan required final approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission. It added it hoped to complete the offer by next April.
The bank said recently in its interim report that a sharp surge in first-half net profits for 1996 was based on its success in expanding its operations.

In an interim report, the bank said that under Chinese accounting standards, it chalked up audited net earnings of 364.23 million yuan in the first half of 1996, compared with 216.50 million yuan in the year-ago period.
